spots.name: Vikings
spots.blurb: You've reached Vikings, a mural by James R. Mayo from 2011. A fully-manned Viking longboat enters Liberty Bay.

spots.name: Uff Da
spots.blurb: You've reached Uff Da, a mural by Wallworks Design Co.. The Norwegian interjection of woe, writ large.

spots.name: Ferry Fever
spots.blurb: You've reached Ferry Fever, a mural by Loc Hong. A massive Sasquatch wearing a purple polka-dotted bathing cap takes a bath in the Sound, while a Washington State Ferry labeled "Ferry Fever" scoots out of the cryptid's way.

spots.name: Untitled mural
spots.blurb: You're at a mural that has been mapped here. Surreal bright graphics: a face with eyes in its hands and chin, a blue head emerging from a box, a head cut into segments, a thumbless hand holding a golden ball, lips with fangs and a green samurai head enjoying the smell of... air conditioning?

spots.name: Silverdale, Mundane and Mythical
spots.blurb: You've reached Silverdale, Mundane and Mythical, a mural. Shows highlights of Silverdale, including a couple of Sasquatches, a boy with a guitar serenading a mermaid, and a flying pig, plus more mundane sights like Clear Creek Trail, Central Kitsap High School, All Star Bowling and a depiction of Whaling Days.

spots.name: Fish
spots.blurb: You've reached Fish, a mural. Colorful fish swimming in blue water.

spots.name: Untitled mural
spots.blurb: You're at a mural that has been mapped here. Painted on the outer walls of the Tracyton Public House in 2004, this mural depicts the beautiful wilderness of the Pacific Northwest.

spots.name: Ugly
spots.blurb: You've reached Ugly, a mural by Bored Waldoe. Personification of Death with a scythe; graffiti-style inscription of the word BORED, additional skull and bones.

spots.name: LOVE
spots.blurb: You've reached LOVE, a mural by Michelle Moshey. Various fruits and vegetables spell out the word LOVE, with a sunrise and a treasure chest full of fresh fruit and veggies.

spots.name: Northwest Logging
spots.blurb: You've reached Northwest Logging, a mural by Ernest Norling. WPA-era mural on the north wall inside the post office, completed in 1938 and restored in the mid-1990s.
